distractors.reason: 'Look for' means search for something. We don't say 'look for the ball' when we only want to see it.
'Look to' means rely on or expect help from someone. It does not describe simply seeing an object.
'Look on' means watch without taking part. It is not used for looking at a red ball.

l1_interference: Türkçede 'bakmak' fiili edat almadan doğrudan nesne alır, bu yüzden 'look the ball' gibi bir hata yapılabilir. İngilizcede doğru kullanım 'look at the ball' şeklindedir.
explanation: In English, 'look' often needs the preposition 'at' when you direct your eyes toward a thing. Turkish speakers may drop the preposition because 'bakmak' takes a direct object.
memory_tip: LOOK AT = point your eyes toward something | LOOK FOR = try to find something
